title: Tortilla Española
subtitle: Spanish potato and egg omelette
excerpt: Spain's most beloved dish: thick slices of potato and onion cooked slowly in olive oil until meltingly soft, then bound with beaten eggs and cooked into a golden omelette that is just barely set in the centre. Served at room temperature.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tortilla española (Spanish omelette) is arguably the most universally eaten dish in Spain; it appears at every bar, café, and home table and is eaten at any hour as a tapa, light meal, or sandwich filling. The dish has two main schools: con cebolla (with onion) and sin cebolla (without onion). The onion camp is the majority view and produces a sweeter, more complex result. The key technique is confiting the potato and onion very slowly in olive oil at a low temperature rather than frying them; this renders them meltingly soft without browning them. The eggs should be just barely set in the centre when the tortilla is removed from the heat. A perfect tortilla should tremble slightly when shaken. It is served at room temperature, not hot.

content.text: The potatoes and onion must cook very slowly in abundant olive oil at a temperature low enough that they bubble gently but do not brown; this takes 20 to 25 minutes and cannot be hurried. The flipping step is the hardest part: use a plate larger than the pan, invert confidently, and slide the tortilla back. A non-stick pan makes the whole process significantly easier.

items.preparation: for confiting; strain and reuse afterwards

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a 24 cm non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the potato and onion with 1 tsp salt. Cook gently, turning occasionally, for 20 to 25 minutes until completely tender and very soft but not browned. Drain, reserving the oil.
Beat the eggs with the remaining salt. Add the potato mixture and stir to combine. Leave to rest for 5 minutes.

Heat 2 tbsp of the reserved oil in the pan over medium heat. Pour in the egg and potato mixture and spread evenly. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the edges are set but the centre is still slightly wobbly. Place a large plate over the pan and invert to flip the tortilla. Slide it back into the pan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more. The centre should still tremble slightly. Rest for 10 minutes before serving at room temperature.
